correctness.rationale: For all n>=3, h_i=(1,i,i^2) gives equality score 1-2(i-j)^2 and strict-order score 2(j-i)-1, so both signed truth matrices have integer margin at least one. The n=1 and n=2 witnesses and 1D order asymmetry establish small cases. For three vectors in dimension <=2 with strictly positive equality diagonal and all negative off-diagonals, all dependence coefficients are nonzero (nonzero proportional pairs contradict signs) and cannot mix signs (positive diagonal would equal negative off-diagonal sum); hence there is a strictly positive dependence. Strict order has negative first column on all three, and applying its column functional to this dependence would imply 0<0. This proves the unrestricted n>=3 lower bound; finite score checks are only corroborative.
